title: Cyrus and the Wolf
premise: Oscar Joubert, a mercenary called the Wolf whose god of oaths has gone silent for a decade, is hired to escort a dying stranger named Cyrus through the Thornfell mountains. Cyrus carries a map inked in dragon-fire and a memory-warded secret: the last dragon's heart still beats beneath Thornfell, and the empire that once hunted dragons has found it. When Cyrus dies mid-journey, his memories bleed into Oscar through an old blood-oath, forcing him to choose between delivering the secret to the smugglers who paid him or destroying it to keep the peace. In the end, Oscar breaks his mercenary contract, binds himself to the dragon's fading fire as its new oath-keeper, and raises a found family of deserters, smugglers, and one imperial defector to guard the mountain — trading his silent god for a living vow.
about_author: Mirabel Voss is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent six seasons mapping passes through ranges she refuses to name, filling notebooks with the stories porters told at night. She writes fantasy about people bound by promises they never meant to keep, and lives somewhere high enough that the mail arrives late.

chapters.title: The God Who Stopped Answering
chapters.summary: Oscar Joubert's POV. Ten years after his oath-god went silent, Oscar takes a routine smuggling job over Thornfell, praying out of habit to nothing. The beat is quiet despair dressed as competence, establishing his hollow loyalty and intimate knowledge of the passes.

chapters.title: A Stranger on the Cold Road
chapters.summary: Oscar finds a wounded man bleeding on the switchbacks above Greywater Ford — Cyrus, pursued by riders wearing no colors. Against every instinct, Oscar carries him. The emotional beat: reluctant compassion overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Map Inked in Fire
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Delirious, Cyrus presses a heat-warm map into Oscar's hands and makes him swear a blood-oath to see it delivered. Oscar feels something answer the oath for the first time in a decade. Beat: dread and a flicker of returned faith.

chapters.title: Riders Without Colors
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The pursuers reach Greywater Ford and burn it, asking questions about a courier. Oscar realizes the job is no longer smuggling; it's survival. Beat: fear hardening into resolve as he chooses the mountain route no one survives.

chapters.title: What Cyrus Remembers
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, fragmented memory chapters: a vault of sleeping dragons, an emperor's order, a theft. He wakes lucid enough to warn Oscar that the map shows where the last dragon's heart still beats. Beat: the weight of witness.

chapters.title: The Widow of Hollowpine
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. They shelter with Sefa, a widow who mends both their gear and their argument about whether to turn back. Sefa feeds them and asks nothing, planting the seed of found family. Beat: warmth in a cold chapter.

chapters.title: Blood-Oath Bleeding
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. His wounds worsen; the blood-oath begins transferring fragments of his memory into Oscar unbidden — a burning library, a child's voice. Oscar resists. Beat: intimacy he never consented to, and cannot refuse.

chapters.title: The Smugglers' Toll
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At the Kestrel Gate, the smuggler-guild chief Brannoc reveals he was the anonymous employer all along and demands the map now. Oscar stalls, lying badly. Beat: loyalty to an old patron curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Imperial Banners in the Pass
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Imperial outriders seal the southern pass; the empire knows what the map shows. Cyrus confesses he stole it from the Emperor's own archive. Beat: the stakes widen from personal to continental.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, flashback-heavy. Why his god went silent, why he stopped believing oaths mean anything — until this one burns in his chest. Beat: confronting the wound beneath his cynicism.

chapters.title: Sefa's Son
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A boy from burned Greywater, Tam, catches up to them seeking revenge on the riders. Oscar tries to send him home; Cyrus quietly takes him in. Beat: the found family forming against Oscar's will.

chapters.title: The First Betrayal
chapters.summary: Brannoc's man among them sells their position. An ambush at the Narrows kills two mules and nearly Cyrus. Oscar executes the traitor and hates how easily his hands remember. Beat: guilt and hardened trust.

chapters.title: Above the Tree Line
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Starving and snowbound, they cross the high shelf where Cyrus teaches Tam the constellations dragons once navigated by. Beat: tenderness as a counterweight to pursuit.

chapters.title: The Silent God Speaks
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Through the blood-oath, Oscar hears not his own god but something older answering — the dragon's heart, dreaming under the stone. Beat: awe and terror; his faith reattaches to the wrong altar.

chapters.title: Brannoc's Ledger
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Captured briefly by Brannoc's men, Cyrus learns the guild intends to sell the map's location to the empire — peace bought with the last dragon. Beat: betrayal by the world's ordinary greed.

chapters.title: Escape Down the Weeping Stair
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A desperate rescue down a frozen waterfall route only Oscar knows. Tam saves Cyrus's life; Oscar stops seeing the boy as baggage. Beat: three strangers becoming a unit.

chapters.title: What Oaths Cost
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The blood-oath deepens: Oscar now remembers Cyrus's childhood, his teacher, his reasons. He argues with a dead man in his own head. Beat: grief arriving before death does.

chapters.title: The Defector
chapters.summary: New POV: Ilsa Vane, an imperial cartographer, defects mid-hunt because she has seen the vault records and knows the war will kill millions. She surrenders to Oscar's knife. Beat: enemy becomes uneasy ally.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Testimony
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Around the fire she lays out the empire's plan: drain the dragon's heart to fuel a new generation of fire-weapons. Cyrus realizes his theft only delayed it. Beat: despair met by Oscar's stubborn 'then we don't let them.'

chapters.title: The Heart Beneath Thornfell
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. They reach the hidden door the map marks. It opens only to dragon-blood or a sworn keeper — and the oath in Oscar's veins turns the lock. Beat: revelation that Oscar was chosen, not hired.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Sleeping Fire
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Descending into the vault, they find the last dragon, ancient and guttering, kept alive by Cyrus's stolen spark. It speaks to each of them differently. Beat: wonder; the secret is alive and afraid.

chapters.title: Cyrus Failing
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Cyrus is dying; the spark keeping the dragon alive will die with him unless someone takes it. The dragon offers it to Oscar. Beat: the choice crystallizes — carry the secret or become it.

chapters.title: Tam's Question
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The boy asks Oscar whether revenge or protection matters more, having watched both fail. Oscar gives no good answer, which is the honest one. Beat: the next generation weighing the same scales.

chapters.title: Brannoc at the Door
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Brannoc's guild and an imperial vanguard arrive together at the vault mouth, uneasy partners. Oscar seals the inner door with the last of the dragon's heat. Beat: siege begins; loyalties fully tested.

chapters.title: The Siege of the Vault
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Days underground: rationing, dark, Ilsa teaching them imperial drill-codes so they can spoof signals. Beat: camaraderie forged in confinement; Ilsa earns her place.

chapters.title: Cyrus's Last Map
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Dying, Cyrus redraws the map from memory and burns the original — the secret can no longer be sold, only carried. He names Oscar keeper. Beat: release; the mission transforms.

chapters.title: The Bargain with Brannoc
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar offers Brannoc the guild's survival instead of the map: sanctuary under the mountain in exchange for turning on the imperials. Brannoc, greedy but pragmatic, wavers. Beat: diplomacy as combat.

chapters.title: The Turning of the Guild
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. The guild votes; half defect to the imperials anyway. Brannoc, choosing poorly all book, finally chooses right — and pays for it. Beat: redemption purchased at cost.

chapters.title: Cyrus Dies at Dawn
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Cyrus dies passing the spark fully into Oscar, who screams with a voice that isn't entirely his own. The mountain answers. Beat: grief and transfiguration entwined.

chapters.title: The Wolf Keeps the Fire
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Transformed as oath-keeper, Oscar can hear the dragon clearly now — and feels the empire's fire-weapons kindling far away. Beat: power with a deadline; the dragon is guttering out.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Message Home
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Using her codes, Ilsa sends false confirmation that the vault is empty, buying time but risking execution if discovered. Beat: quiet courage; truth weaponized carefully.

chapters.title: The Empire Breaks the Door
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The imperial vanguard storms the outer vault; the battle is brutal, close, and lit by dying dragon-fire. Tam kills his first man and comes apart in Oscar's arms. Beat: war's true face.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: The dragon's POV (brief, alien). The last dragon prepares to spend its final fire either destroying the army or seeding a new egg. It asks its keeper to choose. Beat: the thematic crux — vengeance or future.

chapters.title: Oscar's Choice
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Remembering Cyrus, Sefa, Tam, Ilsa — everything built, not burned — Oscar chooses the egg. The dragon pours its last fire into a single stone heart rather than a holocaust. Beat: climax of values.

chapters.title: Fire and Ash at Thornfell
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The spent fire collapses the pass, burying the imperial force and sealing the vault. Brannoc dies holding the gate. Beat: costly victory; the mountain itself becomes the guardian.

chapters.title: Aftermath: Counting the Living
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. They bury the dead, including Cyrus beside the sealed door. Oscar swears a new oath aloud — not to a silent god but to the people around him. Beat: mourning resolving into commitment.

chapters.title: The Egg in the Dark
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Deep in the vault, the stone heart quickens. Tam, who asked the right questions, is the first it trusts. Beat: hope embodied in the youngest character.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa drafts and burns her final report, choosing exile with the found family over return. Sefa arrives at the mountain with supplies and stays. Beat: each character formally choosing belonging.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Vow
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar formalizes the compact: smugglers, deserter, cartographer, widow, boy — wardens of Thornfell. His old god's silence no longer aches. Beat: resolution of the loyalty-vs-truth theme.

chapters.title: Cyrus and the Wolf
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, epilogue. A year later, spring returns to the high passes. Something small and winged stirs beneath the stone, and Oscar — the Wolf who keeps the fire — smiles for the first time in ten years. Beat: quiet, earned hope.
